Somos nanotecnologos interesados la investigación y la aplicación de la ciencia para resolver problemas reales. 

Me gustaría aportar mis conocimientos de química y ciencia de materiales al reto, además de aprender sobre combustión e inteligencia artificial. Busco compañeros con habilidades en programación, análisis de datos, física, química o ingeniería, que tengan iniciativa, compromiso y disposición para colaborar y compartir ideas.
summary:
We developed an educational podcast consisting of 7 episodes titled “Does Anyone Remember Me?”. It is divided into two sections: three episodes dedicated to devices that explored the Moon and four focused on those that traveled to Mars. The project aims to tell the stories of devices sent into space by NASA that, after completing their missions, remained far away from Earth.

The idea is to tell each story from a first-person perspective, giving the devices their own voices, personalities, and even a sense of humor, as if they were remembering their adventures, challenges, and discoveries. This approach allows us to explore topics related to space exploration, technology, and science through entertaining and easy-to-follow stories, while still including important scientific information.

The project aims to bring science closer to children and young people, spark their curiosity about the universe, and show that learning about space exploration can also be a fun and different experience.
details: Our project is an educational podcast called “Does anyone Remember Me?”. It consists of seven episodes: three focused on objects that explored the Moon and four dedicated to devices that traveled to Mars. Each episode tells the story of a real space exploration device developed or sent by NASA. How does it work? The podcast gives each space device its own voice and personality, allowing it to tell its story in the first person, as if it were speaking directly to the audience. Each episode explains what the object is, why it was created, what happened during its mission, the challenges it faced, and what it contributed to space exploration. Instead of presenting the information as a traditional science lesson, we use conversations, humor, sarcasm, and entertaining stories to make the content easier to understand and more engaging. Benefits and expected impact The main benefit is that the podcast makes scientific information more accessible and enjoyable, especially for children and young people. It encourages listeners to learn about space, discover the history of NASA missions, and develop an interest in science and technology. Our expected impact is to inspire curiosity about the universe and help people understand that even objects that may seem forgotten played an important role in expanding our knowledge of space. Tools and technology The project is developed as an audio podcast. Research and scriptwriting are essential parts of its creation, using information about real space missions and reliable sources, particularly NASA materials. No programming languages or specialized hardware are required for the podcast concept itself. Specific recording equipment or audio-editing software can be included according to the tools used during production. Creativity and team considerations The creative aspect of our project is the way we tell the stories. Rather than having astronauts, scientists, or planets explain space exploration, we give the main role to the devices themselves. Each one has a different personality, attitude, and way of speaking, making the episodes feel like conversations with real characters. When developing the project, our team considered the target audience, the accuracy of the scientific information, the length and organization of the episodes, and the importance of keeping the stories entertaining without losing their educational value. Our goal is to combine real facts with creativity and humor, showing that science can be interesting, accessible, and fun.
